I have been farming this land in Quzhou my whole life. My body is not what it used to be at 69 — my sons have moved to the city, so it is just me and my wife. I cannot manage as many mu as before. I will farm my 6 mu this year, the same as last year.

Here in Quzhou, there is only one real choice: winter wheat then summer maize on the same fields. My father grew it, I grow it. It is what the land is suited for, what the buyers at the grain station want, and what I know how to do without any help.

For wheat, I will plant the government-promoted seed variety — the extension station has been pushing improved seeds for years and I have seen they yield better than the old local varieties. I plant in October after preparing the soil with the hand-held rotary tiller I rent. I will water four times: once before winter sets in, once at jointing, once at heading, and once during grain fill. Water is getting harder to come by with the well going deeper every year, but I cannot risk the crop. I apply my base fertilizer — compound fertilizer — at planting and top up urea at jointing. I spray herbicide in spring and watch for rust. Two spray rounds is usually enough.

After wheat harvest in June, I go straight into maize — no time to till, I just direct seed the hybrid into the stubble. Hybrid maize seed is standard now; everyone uses it. Maize only needs water once or twice since the summer rains help. I apply urea twice — once early, once at tasseling.

I expect around 450 jin per mu for wheat and 500 jin per mu for maize. It is not exceptional but it is steady and I know what to do.
